Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset, severe left-sided headache beginning ~4 hours ago this morning; rated 6/10 pain.
- Associated symptoms: Blurred vision with “zig-zag” lines, dizziness, nausea, two episodes of vomiting; worsens with movement; unable to tolerate screens.
- Prior episodes: No similar headaches previously.
- Medications tried today: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) taken ~3 hours ago without relief.
- Past medical history: Previous kidney stones.
- Family history: Mother—migraines, hypothyroidism.
- Medications: None.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies (NKDA).
- Social history: Not discussed.
- Pregnancy: Patient believes pregnancy unlikely.

Objective:
- Telehealth visit—no direct examination performed.
- Patient reports:
  • Able to ambulate normally; no limb weakness, speech changes, or other focal neurological deficits.
- No vital signs or other physical findings documented.
- Investigations: None performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute unilateral headache with visual disturbance
   - Assessment: Probable migraine with aura.
   - Differential: Cluster headache, intracranial hemorrhage/mass, TIA/stroke.
   - Investigations planned: Same-day in-person review for full neurological examination; further imaging only if atypical features develop.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Advise ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) ± over-the-counter anti-emetic.  
     • Encourage intake of sugary carbonated drink (e.g., cola).  
     • Escalate to specific migraine medications if inadequate response.  
   - Safety-net: Attend ED urgently if new neurological deficits, escalating pain to 10/10, persistent vomiting, or no improvement after medication trial.

2. Health anxiety regarding serious intracranial pathology
   - Assessment: Patient worried about brain tumor or stroke.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Reassurance on likely benign etiology.  
     • Education on migraine variability and typical features.  
     • Offer follow-up appointment cancellation option if symptoms resolve; otherwise keep same-day review.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: No vitals, neurological exam findings, social history details (smoking, alcohol, occupation), medication reconciliation (OTC supplements), pregnancy testing not performed.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; brief connectivity issue but did not affect clinical content.
